proxy-intercept.name: Proxy Intercept (Admin Login)
proxy-intercept.description: Learn how to use the Mini Proxy Interceptor to modify a request in transit.

steps.text: Welcome to the Proxy Intercept tutorial! First, we need to navigate to the Login page. Click the 'Account' button in the top navigation bar.
Click 'Login' to go to the authentication page.
In the Email field, type a regular admin email: admin@juice-sh.op
Type any password in the Password field.
Before you click Log in, ensure the Intercept is ON in your Mini Proxy window. Then click 'Log in'.

The request has been paused! Look at the Mini Proxy Intercept window. You'll see the raw HTTP POST request. Find the email parameter in the body and change it to admin@juice-sh.op'--. Then click Forward!

sqli-login.name: SQL Injection (Admin Login)
sqli-login.description: Learn how to bypass authentication using a SQL Injection vulnerability.

steps.text: Welcome to the SQL Injection tutorial! First, we need to navigate to the Login page. Click the 'Account' button in the top navigation bar.
Great! Now click 'Login' to go to the authentication page.
We're on the login page. In the Email field, we will inject a SQL payload. Type exactly: admin@juice-sh.op'--
The single quote (') closes the SQL string early, and the dashes (--) comment out the rest of the query (including the password check). Now click into the Password field.
Since the password check is commented out by our payload, you can type any random password here. Type 'password'.
Perfect! The database will ignore the password. Click the 'Log in' button to execute the attack.

sqli-bender.name: SQL Injection (Bender Login)
sqli-bender.description: Use the same SQLi technique to compromise another user account.

steps.text: Let's compromise Bender's account using the same SQL Injection technique. Click the 'Account' button.
Click 'Login' to go to the authentication page.
In the Email field, target Bender's account. Type exactly: bender@juice-sh.op'--
Now click into the Password field.
Type any password — it will be ignored by the database.
Click 'Log in' to access Bender's account!

sqli-error.name: Error-Based SQL Injection
sqli-error.description: Provoke a database error to confirm SQL injection vulnerability exists.

steps.text: We can confirm SQL injection exists by intentionally breaking a query. Click the search icon in the top bar.
A single quote (') usually breaks SQL syntax. Type a single quote character: '
Before we press Enter, ensure Intercept is OFF on your Mini Proxy. Then press Enter in the search box to trigger the search.
The UI handles the error silently, but if you look at the raw network response, you'll see a SQLITE_ERROR. This proves the backend is directly concatenating your input into SQL!

score-board.name: Find the Score Board
score-board.description: The Score Board is hidden. We need to find the correct path.

steps.text: The Score Board link is not in the menu. But we can navigate to it directly if we know the path. Click the search button to open the search bar.
Instead of searching, we will just manually change the URL. Actually, for this tutorial, I'll reveal the path: it's /#/score-board. Click anywhere to continue.
Let's use the search box to trigger it anyway. Type 'score-board'.
Press Enter to search. Then we will manually navigate there.

xss-search.name: Reflected XSS (Search)
xss-search.description: Execute a basic Cross-Site Scripting attack via the Juice Shop search field.

steps.text: We will test the search functionality for XSS. Look at the top navigation bar and click the magnifying glass search icon.
A search bar has appeared. Type the XSS payload exactly: <iframe src="javascript:alert(`xss`)">
Now press Enter to execute the search. The payload will be reflected into the page and trigger XSS!

Look at the search results area — if you see an embedded iframe or the page behaves unexpectedly, that confirms a Reflected XSS vulnerability! The application did not sanitize your input before rendering it. Click anywhere to finish.

xss-dom.name: DOM-Based XSS
xss-dom.description: Trigger XSS via client-side DOM manipulation without server involvement.

steps.text: DOM XSS happens entirely in the browser — no server involved. Click the search icon in the top navigation.
This time we use the same iframe payload, but the attack vector is different. Angular's client-side router reflects the URL hash directly into the DOM. Type: <iframe src="javascript:alert(`xss`)">
Press Enter. Since the search query is included in the URL hash, Angular processes it locally and renders your payload into the DOM — triggering DOM-based XSS!
DOM-based XSS is harder to detect because the malicious payload never reaches the server — it's processed entirely by client-side JavaScript. Click anywhere to finish.

idor-basket.name: IDOR: View Another Basket
idor-basket.description: Exploit an Insecure Direct Object Reference to view another user's shopping basket.

steps.text: Log in first (you can use your SQLi skills!). Once logged in, click your Basket icon.
Now, ensure Intercept is ON in your Mini Proxy.
Add any item to your basket to trigger a request.
Look at the intercepted request. You will see your basket ID in the URL or Body. Change that ID to '1' or '2' and click Forward!

nmap-basic.name: Basic Scan & Ping Sweep
nmap-basic.description: Learn how to use ping sweeps and basic scans to discover hosts.

steps.text: Welcome to the Nmap Simulator! Let's start by checking if our local machine is responding to pings. Type: ping 127.0.0.1
Great! Now press Enter to execute the ping command.
The host is up. Now let's run a basic Nmap scan on it to see what ports are open. Type: nmap 127.0.0.1
Press Enter to scan.

nmap-sv.name: Service Version Detection
nmap-sv.description: Learn how to use the -sV flag to detect service versions.

steps.text: A basic scan shows open ports, but we need to know exactly what software is running. Type: nmap -sV 127.0.0.1
Press Enter to execute the version scan.

nmap-aggressive.name: Aggressive Scan (-A)
nmap-aggressive.description: Combine OS detection, version detection, script scanning, and traceroute.

steps.text: The -A flag is the 'Aggressive' scan. It runs multiple advanced scans at once. Type: nmap -A 127.0.0.1
Press Enter to execute the aggressive scan.

hydra-ssh.name: SSH Brute Force Attack
hydra-ssh.description: Learn how to use Hydra to brute force an SSH login with a password list.

steps.text: Welcome to the Hydra Simulator! Let's start with an SSH brute force attack. First, type 'hydra' to see the usage help.
Press Enter to see Hydra's help output.
Now let's attack an SSH server. We need: -l for the username, -P for the password file, and the target as ssh://IP. Type: hydra -l root -P rockyou.txt ssh://192.168.1.1
Press Enter to launch the brute force attack!
Hydra found the password! In a real scenario, the green line shows the cracked credentials. The -V flag shows every attempt. Try: hydra -l root -P rockyou.txt ssh://192.168.1.1 -V
Press Enter to see verbose mode — each password attempt is logged.

hydra-http.name: HTTP Form Brute Force
hydra-http.description: Learn how to brute force a web application login form using Hydra's http-post-form module.

steps.text: Web application login forms are common brute force targets. Hydra uses the http-post-form module for this. Type the command: hydra -l admin@juice-sh.op -P rockyou.txt localhost http-post-form "/rest/user/login:{\"email\":\"^USER^\",\"password\":\"^PASS^\"}:Invalid"
Press Enter to attack the Juice Shop login endpoint!

hydra-ftp.name: FTP Brute Force Attack
hydra-ftp.description: Learn how to brute force an FTP server login using Hydra.

steps.text: FTP servers are another common brute force target, especially on legacy systems. The syntax is simple — just change the protocol to ftp://. Type: hydra -l admin -P rockyou.txt ftp://192.168.1.1
Press Enter to launch the FTP brute force attack!
